column1: IDM232 recipe data
40 recipes from the professor's PDFs (pdf1.zip + pdf2.zip), with the gaps filled in by AI. Every PDF-sourced value was checked against the PDFs.
The sheets, in order

recipes_flat: everything about a recipe on one row, enough to build the whole site from this sheet alone: text, ingredient list, tool (name, brand, description, photos), tip, every step with its photos, and every image path. It is built from the other sheets.
recipes: one row per recipe. recipe_id is the primary key; slug is the URL name for your PHP pages and the name of the recipe's image folder.
ingredients: one row per ingredient line, linked by recipe_id. sort_order keeps the list order. quantity, unit and name split the line; full_text is the line as printed.
steps: one row per cooking step, linked by recipe_id and ordered by step_number.
tools: each kitchen tool once, with brand, description and up to 3 photos (image, image_2, image_3).
recipe_tools: links each recipe to its tool (recipe_id + tool_id).
images: every picture the site uses (dish, all-ingredients photo, step photos, tip pictures, tool photos), labeled, with its original file name.
extra_images: every file parked in an extras/ folder (single-ingredient photos, tip thumbnails, wine labels, website graphics, duplicate downloads). Not used by the site; kept so nothing is lost.
tips: the tip each recipe page shows (one per recipe at most), with its picture. tip_type is how_to (print "How To: " before the title) or ingredient_spotlight.
data_notes: what each PDF was missing and what was done about it. Use it for your README's "AI use" section; not a database table.
Gray italic recipe_title / tool_name columns are only there to make browsing easier; leave them out of the SQL tables.
AI-filled data
The PDFs were printed from web pages, and content that fell on a page break was dropped. Your professor said to fill the gaps yourself or with AI, so the gaps are filled.
Filled by AI: 135 ingredient lines, 71 step titles, 18 whole steps (including 3 recipes that only had a title and description), one description, and tools for those 3 recipes.
The source column on ingredients, steps and recipe_tools says where each row came from: pdf, ai, or pdf+ai_title (PDF instructions with an AI-written title).
AI ingredient quantities are estimates based on the steps and the serving size. That is handy for your README's "AI use" section.
category (main protein) and servings were added to recipes for filtering. servings comes from the photo file codes (FP = family plan, 4 servings; 2P = 2 servings).
The "kitchen tools" are the products each recipe page promoted, not a complete list of equipment.
Images
Paths start with images/ and match the images-renamed folder made by rename_map_v2.csv (rename it to images and put it next to your PHP files).

Each recipe folder (named after its slug) holds exactly the pictures its PDF shows: dish.jpg, ingredients.png, step-1.jpg (step-1@2x.jpg is the retina version), tip.jpg, tool-1.jpg / tool-2.jpg. images/tools/ has one copy of each tool's photos for the tools table. Everything else is in the recipe's extras/ folder under its original name.

Step, tip and tool pictures were matched to the PDF pictures pixel by pixel. Spicy Pork uses one photo for steps 4 and 6, as its PDF does; Tuscan step 5 has no photo. The 3 recipes with no steps in their PDFs had their photos ordered by eye and their AI steps adjusted to fit.
For SQL and PHP
Primary keys: recipes.recipe_id, ingredients.ingredient_id, steps.step_id, tools.tool_id, tips.tip_id, images.image_id. recipe_tools uses (recipe_id, tool_id) together.
Foreign keys: ingredients, steps, tips, images and recipe_tools point at recipes.recipe_id; recipe_tools.tool_id points at tools.tool_id.
A recipe page: look up the recipe by slug, then pull its ingredients (ORDER BY sort_order), steps (ORDER BY step_number), tip and tool by recipe_id.
Search and filter: title, subtitle, description and ingredients.name are the text to search; category is the filter.
quantity is display text ("1½"), not a number.
recipes_flat, extra_images and data_notes are for reading, not importing.
Version history
ver3: audited against the PDFs; fixed Seared Steaks step 3 source, General Tso's step 2 period, added Pimento's Sweet Potato tip.
ver4: step photos put in PDF order by pixel matching.
ver5: clean image names; tool and tip pictures matched to the PDFs; the 3 photo-only recipes use the Large Maple Cutting Board, the tool in their folders.
ver6: removed empty columns, straight quotes, tip_type, needs_review renamed data_notes.
ver7: plain tool_images paths, image labels, cells sized to their contents.

ver8: images holds only pictures the site uses, the rest moved to extra_images; recipes_flat rebuilt with tool brand, tool description, tip_type and ingredient_count so it covers the whole site; sheets reordered.
